text: OVERDOSAGE Symptoms: Overdosage may cause hallucinations, convulsions, CNS depression, cardiovascular collapse and death. Overdosage with dextromethorphan HBr may produce nausea and vomiting, central nervous system excitement and mental confusion, visual disturbances, and urinary retention. Very high doses may produce respiratory depression. One case of toxic psychosis (hyper-reactivity, marked visual and auditory hallucinations) after a single 300 mg dose of dextromethorphan has been reported. Treatment: Treatment of overdosage should provide symptomatic care. If the amount ingested is considered dangerous or excessive, induce vomiting with ipecac syrup unless the patient is convulsing, comatose, or has lost the gag reflex, in which case perform gastric lavage using a largebore tube. If indicated, follow with activated charcoal and a saline cathartic. Since the effects of this product may last up to 12 hours, treatment should be continued for at least that length of time.
